ruleName: Order of Play in Stroke Play
title: Who plays first when one ball is on the green and another in a bunker closer to the hole?
question: In a stroke play competition, your ball is on the putting green. Your playing partner's ball is in a bunker, but it is closer to the hole than yours. Who should play first?

choices.text: You should play first because your ball is already on the putting green.
Your partner should play first because their ball is farther from the hole.
Your partner should play first because their ball is farther from the hole.
You can choose who plays first.

explanation: The order of play in stroke play is determined by which ball is farther from the hole, not by which area of the course the ball is in. Even if one ball is on the green and another elsewhere, the player whose ball is farther away plays first. Ready Golf is encouraged in stroke play to improve pace of play, but there is no penalty for playing out of turn. In this scenario, since your ball is on the green and your partner's ball is in a bunker closer to the hole, you (with the ball farther from the hole) should play first.
